title: Bitcoin AI Model Review — Week 44: 1 of 5 Calls Correct
meta_description: Week 44 graded: 1 of 5 Bitcoin calls correct (20%). All-time: 37.9% over 87 public calls. Paper portfolio +10.2% vs holding.

intro: Welcome to the QuantAura Signals weekly recap reviewing every graded call for the date range 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30.
The model logged a particularly poor performance with only 1 hit out of 5 resolved calls this week for a 20.0 percent accuracy rate.
The system closed out the period on a 3 call miss streak after failing on four of the five trading sessions.
days: On Monday, the algorithm opened with a sell signal at 82.4 percent confidence, but the market moved opposite as price rose 1.13 percent.
Tuesday delivered the single correct hit of the week when a hold prediction with 67.6 percent confidence matched a slight 0.46 percent move.
On Thursday, another hold call at 61.6 percent confidence resulted in a miss when Bitcoin dropped 2.77 percent.
On Friday, the model issued a high confidence sell signal at 93 percent, yet price went up 1.16 percent to cap off a rough stretch.
spotlight: Wednesday stood out as the notable call of the week and served as the clearest mistake in the dataset.
The model output a hold call at 82.2 percent confidence, expecting price movement to remain quiet over the 24 hour horizon.
Instead, Bitcoin fell by 2.82 percent, breaking far outside the 1.0 percent flat band and grading this call as a clear miss.
trend: Market price action started with small gains early in the week before shifting into consecutive downward drops on Wednesday and Thursday.
Bitcoin closed the week with a minor move back upward on Friday, completely opposing the model signals along the way.
portfolio: The paper trading portfolio started at 10000.0 dollars and now stands at 11014.61 dollars after 89 days and 10 trades, resulting in a 10.15 percent return while sitting in cash.
A simple buy and hold benchmark over the identical timeframe reached a value of 12045.02 dollars, generating a 20.45 percent return.
Account fees took 163.2 dollars, meaning taking these signals underperformed buy and hold by -10.3 percent.
record: Looking at the macro picture, the all time record sits at 33 hits out of 87 resolved calls, producing an overall accuracy of 37.9 percent.
The model has struggled even more recently, with the thirty day metric showing an accuracy of 32.1 percent across 28 resolved calls.
Evaluating performance by signal type reveals that sell signals have achieved only 9.7 percent accuracy across 31 calls.
Because the overall sample size remains relatively small, we present these raw results without filtering out the bad runs.

research.title: Why the model sometimes refuses to call a direction
paragraphs: When the ensemble's confidence falls below its threshold, a gate downgrades the call to hold.
A forced guess would look decisive and grade like a coin flip. The gate would rather say nothing.
That makes hold the most common call here, and it is meant to be. A model with a strong opinion every single day is telling you about itself rather than about the market.
